paper_verdict.estimator_family: Cross-section OLS (MRW-augmented, bootstrap SEs), panel fixed effects, and G2SLS with fixed effects (lagged ICT instruments); growth regressions are cross-section OLS
paper_verdict.pooling_concerns: Mixed outcome units: Tables 1-2 use ln GDP per working-age person (level), Table 3 uses log difference 1985-97 (growth), so Table 3 estimates should not be pooled with level estimates. ICT exposure differs across rows: composite index vs single indicators (phones, mobile, PCs), log initial level vs average growth rate gICT (semi-elasticity). Overlapping samples (1983-97 vs 1991-97, same countries) and many specifications from the same data. Working paper; reverse causality handled only by lagging (initial ICT level) and G2SLS with lagged internal instruments.

paper_verdict.estimator_family: DOLS (dynamic OLS with leads and lags of first differences) panel with country and sector fixed effects, year dummies or time trend
paper_verdict.pooling_concerns: Outcome is estimated ln TFP level (generated dependent variable from AMG production-function estimation), not output per worker. ICT exposure is ln of the contribution of ICT capital services to value added growth (EU KLEMS), a growth-accounting contribution not an ICT stock or intensity, so the coefficient is not a standard elasticity. The 3 estimates are one regression (two FE variants plus a standardized beta, which has different units). Sector-level manufacturing data, 17 EU countries, 1995-2007. Coefficients on a different scale from output elasticities of ICT capital.
